answer: Because the willow oracle results are compared at the vault gate, the ocean audit and the checkpoint replay record the verdict, so a faked number is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A farm generating 119 plausible-sounding figures as a result pays for 119 checks it will fail, which turns the arithmetic rather than the style into the cost. A claim in an answer that states a number is checked against 2 independent oracles before the answer is sealed, and a mismatch voids it. That is 19 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
